assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase from the same period last year, and Wikipedia readership is at the 99th percentile of the past year.
Polio cases are peaking with a 96th percentile of Wikipedia readership and a reported cluster of four cases in Syria.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with an 853% increase from the same period last year, and news coverage is 1.2x its previous four weeks.
Influenza cases are peaking with a 22% increase in global flu test positivity and 55% more US hospital admissions than last month.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with an 87% increase from the same period last year, and news coverage is 1.6x its previous four weeks.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a 55% increase from the same period last year, and news coverage is 2.3x its previous four weeks.
West Nile virus cases in the US are rising with a 1388% increase from the same period last year, and Wikipedia readership is at the 0th percentile of the past year.
Covid-19 hospital admissions in the US are at baseline with a 13% increase from last month, and Wikipedia readership is at the 12th percentile of the past year.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising, with a 45% increase in the 8-week average compared to the previous 8 months, and over 8,000 cases reported this year.
Chikungunya cases in the US remain stable, with 282 cases reported this year compared to 259 last year, but Switzerland reported its first locally acquired cases in October 2026.
Global RSV test positivity is up 17% this week compared to last month, with US hospital admissions increasing by 57% in the past month.
Norovirus news coverage is increasing, with about 5 English articles per day reported in the last 4 weeks.
Hepatitis A cases in the US are up 10% compared to the previous 8 months, with 630 cases reported this year.
Malaria cases in the US are up 30% compared to the previous 8 months, with 1,161 cases reported this year.
Cholera news coverage is increasing, with about 16 English articles per day reported in the last 4 weeks.
